key_insight: Recasting neural quantum state training as a reinforcement-learning-style trust-region problem leads to a more stable and scalable optimizer for variational wavefunction learning.
engineering_relevance: The proposed Proximal Wavefunction Optimization (PWO) offers a practical first-order alternative to costly, fragile stochastic reconfiguration for large-scale quantum many-body simulations.
method: View energy minimization as advantage policy-gradient optimization over the Born distribution
Clip amplitude probability ratios and phase increments separately to form a trust region
Reuse samples across multiple updates while avoiding explicit matrix inversion
evidence_signal: In experiments on Ising and frustrated J1-J2 spin systems, PWO showed improved stability and wall-clock convergence over Adam, minSR, and SPRING, and it was also used to fine-tune a 1.5B-parameter RWKV-7 model.
watch_item: As with other trust-region and sampling-based methods, performance may depend on careful tuning of clipping ranges and numerical stability in high-dimensional, phase-sensitive models.
paper_title: One More Time: Revisiting Neural Quantum States from a Reinforcement Learning Perspective
